question: Why is space cold if the Sun is hot?
short_answer: Space is a vacuum containing very few molecules to absorb or transfer heat. Temperature measures kinetic energy of matter, so empty space itself has no conventional temperature.
full_explanation: Objects in space absorb solar radiation directly, reaching high temperatures on their sunlit sides while dropping to near absolute zero in shadowed regions.
